A QuickGUI project keeps application code in a Go module and development commands in a small Bun package.

## Generated files

The CLI generates these files. Commit `go.sum` after resolving dependencies.

```text
my-app/
├── main.go
├── go.mod
├── go.sum
├── quickgui.config.ts
├── package.json
└── README.md
```

## Application entry

`main.go` starts `native.Run` and creates a window. Components and children blocks share the `func()` signature and declare their children in order, without returning a node. Split larger applications into ordinary Go packages.

```go
func ViewExample() {
	ui.View(
		func() {
			ui.Text("Hello from Go")
			ui.Button("Continue", ui.OnClick(func() {}))
		},
		ui.Padding(20),
		ui.Gap(12),
	)
}
```

## Configuration

`entry` is the Go package to build. The configuration file is evaluated by the Bun CLI. It is not part of the running application.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@quickgui/cli";

export default defineConfig({
  name: "My App",
  identifier: "com.example.my-app",
  entry: ".",
});
```

You can also use `quickgui.toml` with the same settings:

```toml
name = "My App"
identifier = "com.example.my-app"
entry = "."

[native]
tags = ["production"]
```

The CLI checks `quickgui.toml` before `quickgui.config.ts`. `quickgui dev --config configs/dev.toml` or `quickgui build --config configs/release.toml` selects a file explicitly. Relative paths are resolved from the project directory, and `dev` reloads config edits. Quote version values, for example `version = "0.1.0"`, and put application fields before the `[native]` table.

## Packages

Use `github.com/egoist/quickgui/go/native` for windows and platform services, `github.com/egoist/quickgui/go/ui` for UI, and `github.com/egoist/quickgui/go/reactive` for owners and contexts. `@quickgui/cli` is a development dependency. Pin the Go SDK and CLI to compatible release versions.

To share your own components or build an optional native backend, see [Authoring Extensions](/docs/go/extensions).
